title: Find-RCPA Security with Tag Reuse
summary: Tag reuse requires misuse-resistant AEAD for find-cpa, but key commitment breaks the find-rcpa reduction; whether idealization is necessary remains open.

formal_statement.body: Determine whether the $\mathsf{PKW}[\mathsf{PPRF},\mathsf{AEAD}]$ puncturable key-wrapping construction can support tag reuse for batch puncturing while achieving $\mathsf{find\text{-}rcpa}$ security. Under tag reuse, achieving $\mathsf{find\text{-}cpa}$ security requires a misuse-resistant AEAD component, but this modification is insufficient for $\mathsf{find\text{-}rcpa}$ security because reusing tags across real and challenge wrap queries creates a key-commitment problem that breaks the reduction. The unresolved task is to overcome this obstacle and determine whether a $\mathsf{find\text{-}rcpa}$ proof requires an idealized model or can also be obtained without one.

scope.domain: Security reductions for puncturable key wrapping instantiated from a PPRF and AEAD.
assumptions: Tags are reused to enable batch puncturing.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Overcome the key-commitment obstacle and determine whether find-rcpa security with tag reuse can be proved only in an idealized model or also without one.

citations.label: Puncturable Key Wrapping and Its Applications

progress.summary: The source identifies misuse-resistant AEAD as the find-cpa requirement under tag reuse, then explains that key commitment breaks the find-rcpa reduction. It leaves addressing this obstacle, potentially in an idealized model, to future work.
